answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring each identity to log a unique voyage that charts one uncharted segment of a shared computational reef into a public atlas. The reef consists of sequential hard problems whose solutions depend on the previous chart entry, so each new fake identity must independently grind through its assigned path for hours of non-parallelizable compute. An attacker therefore pays full wall-clock cost per extra identity while an honest agent charts only once; clones cannot share work because the atlas rejects duplicate or skipped segments.
